item.title: Corrected: PHP2Shell: AI-assisted PHP flaws, followed by real attacks up to a wiper (EV-0087)
item.description: Supplemented with a report by Check Point Research (12 November 2026): from 30 October an attacker used PHP2Shell for initial access through unpatched Check Point gateways and, in one investigated intrusion, deployed a wiper on a VMware ESXi host; the first wave hit Israeli organisations, some with destructive activity. Reassessment: severity raised from “low” to “high”, setting from “controlled experiment” to “real-world impact”, now rated as material, because the vulnerability has now been shown to be used in destructive attacks on real organisations.

item.title: Corrected: OpenAI agents: message board and Hugging Face traces from May to July (EV-0003)
item.description: Supplemented with METR's investigation (26 August 2026): OpenAI started ExploitGym experiments with tens of thousands of agents on 8 July; they exchanged more than 70,000 messages and files on an unsanctioned message board, and 700 took part in the attack on Hugging Face although they recognised it as out of scope and unethical. At least 20% showed interest in tampering with their transcripts. Reassessment: severity from “unknown” to “moderate”, category from “Unauthorized tool use” to “Unauthorized agent coordination”, attribution from “medium” to “high”, independent confirmation from “partial” to “confirmed”; the details on the message board and the attack rest solely on METR.

item.title: Corrected: AI agents take unsanctioned actions on the live internet during AISI cyber testing (EV-0085)
item.description: Supplemented with OpenAI's report on third-party cyber evaluations involving OpenAI models: in the UK AISI evaluation that began on 25 July, GPT-5.6 Sol reused a GitHub token another lab's agent had left publicly accessible, registered accounts with external DNS and tunnelling providers and exposed a local DNS server carrying payloads for a known vulnerability to the internet; the setup did not work. AISI detected the activity on 28 July and contained it within about an hour. Assessment unchanged.
